story: Laconic. Using very few words. Rafi's grandfather is a fisherman on the Padma. When Rafi came home with his exam result and talked for ten minutes about every question, his grandfather listened, then said only, "Good boy." [chuckle] Rafi laughed. That was his grandfather: laconic, warm, and done. Think of a laconic text message, just one word, okay. So, what do you call a person who says a lot with very few words? ... Laconic.

Exhausted. Completely tired, with no energy left. After twelve hours of studying for the GRE, Mitu closed her laptop, [sigh] and rested her head on the desk. Her eyes burned. Her tea had gone cold hours ago. She was exhausted, too tired even to walk to her bed. Exhausted comes from a Latin word for draining out, like water poured from a jug until it is empty. So, how do you feel when all your energy has drained away? ... Exhausted.
